messages:
maria: heads up — saw a ~3x spike in fncall schema rejections in us-west canary starting ~10:12 UTC. Breaking a few customer flows. :eyes:
ajay: ugh. any example errors? are these strict-validate rejects or parse failures?
maria: strict-validate. sample log: 
```
2026-03-23T10:13:02Z validator=v2 fncall_id=abc123 route=canary-usw outcome=REJECT reason=TYPE_MISMATCH field=metadata.timestamp expected=string got=number
```
ajay: thanks. that reason code is helpful. looks like the canary model started returning ints for timestamps in some batch paths. is this only for tools that expect RFC3339?
maria: yes, mostly timestamp + some numeric ids where schema expects string enums. Also noticed routing fallback to the degen/text route for ~40% of those requests — which means extra tokens billed and different QA.
sam: does fallback increment quota for the original route or the degen route? that affects billing attribution and quota exhaustion.
ajay: current behavior: validator rejects, orchestration reroutes to fallback route (degen), request is billed under fallback route id. so quota/usage shows under degen. This leads to undercounting rejects on the original route and misattributed billing.
maria: that's the core problem. ops saw increased token spend but the canary route quota didn't reflect it. customers confused.
dev-console: we can add a dashboard column for 'final_route' vs 'origin_route' and a filter for validation.reason_code, but we need a stable field name to index. propose: fncall.validation.reason_id and routing.final_route_id. Thoughts?
ajay: reason_id sounds good. prefer enum-style strings (e.g., TYPE_MISMATCH, MISSING_REQUIRED, UNEXPECTED_ARRAY). Also add a boolean fncall.validation.soft_fail to indicate permissive fallback.
sam: long-term: orchestration should emit a tagged metric like fncall.fallback.via_validator with labels {origin_route, final_route, reason}. That lets SRE/finance reconcile cost. Short-term we need a fix for canary.
maria: short-term mitigation options: 1) flip validator to soft-mode for canary (allow passthrough + tag) 2) pin canary model to previous build 3) block reroute and surface an error to client (bad UX). I'm leaning to (1) until we finish root cause.
ajay: soft-mode plus tagging is reasonable. but we must ensure we still sample full payloads for debugging — increase DLQ sampling from 1% to 25% for this slice.
dev-console: UI-wise we'll expose a toggle in rollouts: "soft-validate on reject" with a tooltip: "allow fallback while tagging validation issues; recommended for canary". I can add a temporary badge in the route list showing active soft-validate + sample rate.
sam: we also need to avoid quota gaming: if soft-validate routes to degen and consumes tokens, customers might circumvent protected quotas. Suggest: when soft-validate is on, increment original route's reject_count and bill to final_route but emit reconciliation metric to attribute cost back to origin_route for billing reports.
ajay: technically feasible: add metric fncall.cost.attributed.{origin_route,final_route}. We'll need a small pipeline change in billing ingest — Finance ok with a reconciliation field.
maria: can we also add a console alert when reject rate > 0.5% AND fallback_rate > 10% for a route during a rollout? customers noticed silent cost spikes because no alert existed.
dev-console: yep. I'll wire a rule: (reject_rate >= 0.005 and fallback_rate >= 0.1) => create alert and show runbook. Need final field names from platform team.
ajay: I'll send a short RFC for the telemetry fields and a migration plan for legacy indices. Will include the reason enum and soft_fail flag.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/us-west/2026-03-23-10:20 (image: inference:1.14.2)
maria: thanks. ajay — can you own short-term soft-mode toggle + metric tags? I'll loop in SE if customers ask.
ajay: on it. will push soft-validate toggle by 10:30 and increase DLQ sampling.
sam: scheduling a 15m post-mortem check at 11:00 to confirm metrics and billing attribution.
dev-console: I'll add the dashboard filter and the temporary badge before 10:45.
maria: perfect. Also adding a short note in the rollout doc about conservative schema stricness for canaries.
ajay: note to self: add automated tests for enum normalization + type coercion in validator v2.
maria: huge help — thanks team :thumbsup:
